claims.text: A lighthouse keeper climbs the tower stairs in a storm and lights the lamp.
No spoken or sung lines are to be added.
The lighthouse stands on a black rock in a heaving sea, and the keeper wears a heavy oilskin coat.
A restrained orchestral score grows slowly beneath the storm and opens as the lamp catches.

description.text: A severe storm fills the night above a cold, churning sea. Rain slants in dense horizontal sheets, and white surf bursts against the black rock beneath a tall stone lighthouse. The tower rises in wet gray masonry, its gallery railing and dark lamp room silhouetted against the cloud mass; the lamp is unlit. Salt spray streaks the lower walls, and the whole structure seems small against the moving water and wind.
Surf explodes high against the rock and rain sweeps across the frame in wind-driven sheets.
Wind howls around the tower while surf crashes and drags over stone.

Inside the lighthouse, a keeper in a heavy oilskin coat climbs a tight spiral staircase of wet iron. One gloved hand grips the curved rail while a shuttered hand lantern swings at the keeper's hip, throwing a small, unsteady pool of warm light across the stone shaft. The stairs coil upward into shadow; draft-driven rain streaks the narrow windows, and the lantern flame flattens and recovers with each step.
The keeper climbs steadily, lantern swinging, boots finding each wet tread.
Iron treads ring under boots, and breath labors in the closed shaft.
A gust moans through the stone and makes the lantern flame gutter.

In the glass-walled lamp room, the keeper sets the lantern on a metal ledge, then grips the brass valve of the lamp mechanism and turns it. The wick catches with a soft bloom; pale flame spreads behind the great faceted lens, and the lens throws a sudden flare across the wet glass. The keeper raises a forearm to shield their eyes as brass, glass, and stone take on a warm, shifting glow.
The keeper turns the valve; the wick catches and the lens flares.
Brass clicks and turns, and a soft whoosh rises as the flame catches.
Glass ticks in its frame under the growing heat.

From outside, the lighthouse now burns at the top of the tower. A long white beam swings out across the storm, cutting through rain and spray in a slow sweep while the keeper’s dark silhouette stands behind the glowing glass. Below, surf continues to break white against the rock; above, the beam reaches into the night and disappears into the cloud.
The beam sweeps out over the storm while the keeper stands silhouetted behind the glass.
A deep rotating hum comes from the lens mechanism.
Wind and surf continue beneath rain ticking on the glass.

soundscape: Diegetic storm: howling wind, crashing surf, rain lashing stone and glass, boots on iron treads, labored breathing, a draft moaning in the shaft, brass valve clicks, a soft flame whoosh, glass ticking, and the deep rotating hum of the lens.
music: A restrained, slow-building orchestral score with low strings, distant brass, and a soft pulse, mixed beneath the diegetic storm; it grows subtly as the lamp catches and opens into a steady, hopeful bed as the beam sweeps out.
